rationale: bugs_open/122 (generated CSS fails WCAG AA on live sites). Re-measured the whole fleet in a browser on 2026-08-06 rather than trusting the file's 07-28 figures: 109 firm contrast failures across 12 of 15 homepages. Two of the file's three findings are FIXED and its first fix candidate has shipped (the shared header-theme-chrome template is now var-driven and 0 of 19 stored header chrome rows carry a hardcoded white CTA ink), so this change targets the class that SURVIVED, which is a different one. Two sub-shapes are addressed here. (A) A palette slot spent on both a FILL and an INK: a dark site's `primary` is a near-background dark, which is correct as a button fill (16.28:1 for light text on it) and invisible as text on the page. 17 of 18 layouts use `color: var(--color-primary)` as an ink, and dartsonline serves .image-hover-card-grid__eyebrow at 1.04:1 while robot-hands serves .tl-eyebrow at 1.14 and .tl-card-link at 1.07 — all from shared, unforked, active component templates. `warnUnusablePrimary` ALREADY DETECTS this exact condition below 3.0 and only logs, and `darkSchemeDerivations` derives `primary_text` (the ink that goes ON a primary fill) but nothing derives the inverse direction: primary made legible as an ink on the page. The platform computes that answer twice already (pickInkOn, pickReadableOnBackground) and never offers it that way round. (B) A component hard-coding white over a themed mid-tone fill (features_open/026 family 3): finetuning .csg-cta-btn white on #C8873A = 3.01, gaswholesalers .A #E8A020 on white = 2.22, gamesdesign .stats-eyebrow #00E5FF on #0DBFD6 = 1.44. The slot for this ALREADY EXISTS and is dead: `accent_text` was added to darkSchemeDerivations on 2026-07-27 with the comment 'It is emitted so a component can stop hard-coding white over an accent fill', and it is declared by 0 of 18 layouts, so it is never emitted and has zero consumers on all five surfaces that could name it. That is the recorded LANDMINE 'a palette slot no LAYOUT declares is never emitted — deriving it is dead config', sitting unfired in the list it was written about. The intent is therefore NOT to add a derivation (that is the mistake the landmine describes) but to make the derived answers REACHABLE from one renderer-owned place, so that a component can opt in with a var() fallback that preserves today's rendering wherever the slot is undefined.

plan.summary: Emit two legible-ink custom properties from the CSS renderer's own :root block — `--color-accent-text` (an existing derived slot that no layout declares, so it has never reached a stylesheet) and `--color-primary-ink` (new: primary made legible as an ink, required to clear AA against BOTH background and surface). Emission is from the renderer, not from 18 layout css_templates, because a palette slot no layout declares is never emitted; and it is scheme-independent, unlike fillDarkSchemeSpecialisedSlots, because two of the three failing sub-shape-B sites are LIGHT. The change is additive and inert: nothing renders differently until a component template writes `var(--color-primary-ink, var(--color-primary))`, so the opt-in is a component author's own edit, visible to a reviewer of the component. Two shared components are then repointed to close the measured instances of sub-shape A.

edits.rationale: The question 'is this colour legible as text on that ground' is answered nowhere in this direction. pickInkOn answers the inverse (what ink goes ON this fill) and pickReadableOnBackground walks a preference order tuned for section body copy. This one takes a source colour and returns it unchanged when it already clears the floor against every ground it must survive, else the first palette colour that does, else black or white — so a site keeps its character wherever the character is legible.

This is the seam that makes the derived answers reachable. It follows the established renderer-owned :root pattern (buildSectionDefaults, buildTokenAliases) rather than adding {{palette}} calls to 18 layout css_templates, because two hand-maintained lists that must stay identical is the drift class this council reviews for, and because a slot no layout declares is never emitted at all. It skips any name the CSS already defines, exactly as buildTokenAliases does, so a layout or theme that has an opinion keeps it.

Wire the block in. It must run AFTER the section defaults and the token aliases are appended, because it tests the assembled css for an existing definition of each name — running it earlier would let a later block silently shadow it and produce exactly the dead-config outcome this change exists to remove.

Four cases, each chosen because it fails a plausible wrong implementation rather than to cover lines. The no-op case is the one that matters most: a fix that repaints sites whose colours are already legible is a regression dressed as a win, and it is the failure mode this bug file explicitly warns about ('findings get fixed into real regressions').

This function already measures the exact condition the new slot repairs, and its comment says it warns rather than fails because 'there is no single correct repair'. That is no longer true — there is now a repair, and the log line should name it, or the next reader re-derives the whole analysis from a warning that offers nothing.

Both are active and unforked; image-hover-card-grid has 1 placement on 1 site, tool-list has 6 placements across 4 sites. The var() fallback means a site whose stylesheet predates the renderer change renders exactly as it does today, so this is safe to apply before every stylesheet has been re-rendered.

plan.risks:
1. THE SCHEME WIDENING IS THE THING TO PUSH ON. fillDarkSchemeSpecialisedSlots is dark-only by a deliberate, documented boundary ('a light literal is only wrong when the site is dark'). buildLegibleInkDefaults deliberately does NOT adopt that boundary, because sub-shape B's failures are on light sites (gaswholesalers #F4F1EB, finetuning #F5F3EF). A reviewer should decide whether emitting on light sites is acceptable; my argument is that legibility of an ink on a ground is scheme-independent whereas a light literal's wrongness is not, and that the emission is inert anyway. Test case 3 pins it so it cannot be silently re-narrowed.
2. ONE VARIABLE, TWO GROUNDS. --color-primary-ink is required to clear AA against background AND surface, because dartsonline places the same ink on both. If a component puts it on a THIRD ground (an accent-filled band), it is not covered and may still fail. That is why accent_text stays a separate slot rather than being folded in. Check: is requiring both grounds too strict on a palette whose background and surface are far apart in lightness — could it force an achromatic fallback and cost a site its character on a page that only ever uses the ink on one of them?
3. IT DETECTS NOTHING NEW AND PREVENTS NOTHING BY ITSELF. This change makes a correct value AVAILABLE; it does not stop the next component hard-coding white. The preventive half is the render audit's cadence (built and live in v1.0.1257, dispatched by nothing — 28 enabled scheduled_tasks, none targeting render-audit-agent, 4 contrast_failure items ever), which is deliberately NOT in this submission because it is live config needing no build. If a seat thinks the two must land together, say so.
4. ORDERING INSIDE THE RENDERER. buildLegibleInkDefaults reads the ASSEMBLED css to decide whether a name is already defined, so it must be appended last. If a future edit moves it earlier, a later :root block could shadow it and the change reverts to dead config with no signal. Worth a reviewer's eye on whether a positional dependency in a 10-step function is acceptable, or whether the guard should assert its own position.
5. THE MIGRATION TOUCHES SHARED COMPONENT TEMPLATES (tool-list: 6 placements, 4 sites; image-hover-card-grid: 1, 1). Sites whose styles.css predates the renderer change fall through to var()'s second argument and render unchanged, so there is no ordering constraint between the two halves — but a reviewer should confirm that reading of the fallback rather than take it from me.
6. NOT ADDRESSED HERE, DELIBERATELY: vonc.com's Gauntlet buttons (23 failures, same shape) belong to the gauntlet_dead_cta lane and 122 says to coordinate; and ai-agent-orchestration.com's six .H3 at 1.00:1 (heading equal to its own background) is filed to the 090 diagnosis loop (run correlation 5853ee07-a49c-4571-8ea0-3eb660e43dfd) because two mechanisms that should prevent it both appear to be in place and I will not guess at the cause.
7. OTHER CONSUMERS OF THIS SEAM, told rather than merely measured: every generated stylesheet gains up to two :root names. The lanes with a stake are brochure_component_library (owns palette_specialised_slots.go and the derivations), dartsonline_traffic (contributed the double-duty finding; its site is a measured instance), oufe (filed 122), webdesign_uk_build_service (recorded the dead-derivation landmine) and gauntlet_dead_cta (same defect shape, surface untouched). What changes for them: nothing renders differently until a component opts in, and a slot they already define is never overwritten.
